You are going to turn a workout into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme workout and deliver a live timeline: Erg Session — four rowers, two machines for 4 rowers, 2 ergs, 3 pieces
Resource limits: two ergs, four rowers, one coach, one rower on the coached drill at a time.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Erg Session — four rowers, two machines

Two ergs in the bay and four of us, so we row in pairs and the pair that is off the machines is the pair that is resting. A and B are the first pair, C and D the second. Nobody sits on a machine they are not rowing.

Warm-up
A and B warm up first: 10 minutes, rate 18, light pressure, half slide to full slide.
C and D come in ten minutes later and take the machines for their own 10 minute warm-up.

The pieces
Three pieces, four minutes each, rate 26 to 28, target split on the monitor.
A and B take the first piece as soon as C and D are off the machines.
C and D take the first piece straight off the back of A and B's first piece.
A and B start their second piece four minutes after their first one ends.
C and D take the second piece as soon as A and B are off.
A and B start their third piece four minutes after their second one ends.
C and D take the third piece as soon as A and B are off.

Technique drill
Three minutes each, one at a time, coach on the machine with you: pause at the finish, pause at half slide, then build. A goes first once C and D are off the last piece, then B, then C, then D.

Cooldown
Ten minutes on the floor together once the last drill is done: legs up the wall, hips, lats, then a cup of tea.

Coach
Brief the crew on the boards before anyone gets on: 5 minutes.
Call splits from the first piece: 20 minutes on the clock, watch the catch not the monitor.
Run the drills: 12 minutes, one rower at a time, straight through.
Debrief after the cooldown: 10 minutes, what the splits said and what Saturday looks like.

Note
The rests are not steps for the first pair: they are the gap between one piece ending and the next one starting, because the machines are handed over in that gap and the second pair is using them. The second pair's rests are the first pair's pieces. That is the whole design of the session.
>>>

**Read-back**

This is a single coached erg session for **four rowers (A, B, C and D) working as two pairs** on **two ergs that exist only twice**, with **one coach** — so at any moment at most two people are on machines and the other pair is *resting*, not idling on equipment they are not rowing. It starts with the coach's 5-minute brief on the boards before anybody gets on; then A and B take the two ergs for a 10-minute warm-up and C and D arrive 10 minutes later for their own 10 minutes. Then three 4-minute pieces per pair (rate 26–28) run as a strict relay: A/B piece 1 → C/D piece 1 straight off the back of it → A/B piece 2 (starting exactly 4 minutes after their piece 1 ended, i.e. the moment C/D come off) → C/D piece 2 → A/B piece 3 → C/D piece 3, so **the off pair's "rest" is deliberately the other pair's piece — that gap is the handover, not a step**. After the last piece, four 3-minute technique drills (pause at the finish, pause at half slide, then build) run **one rower at a time with the coach on the machine** — A, then B, then C, then D, 12 minutes straight through — followed by a 10-minute cooldown together on the floor and a 10-minute debrief; the coach also calls splits from the first piece for 20 minutes on the clock. **No finishing time was given**, so the program should simply make the whole thing finish as early as the work allows (roughly 80 minutes from the brief, if nothing queues behind an erg or the coach). The source text is complete — all six sections (warm-up, pieces, drill, cooldown, coach, note) are present; the only fuzziness I'll flag is that the coach's "20 minutes" of split-calling from the first piece doesn't quite cover all six pieces (those span 24 minutes), so I'll treat the coach step as the stated 20 minutes.

A **track** is one sequential line of work — effectively one person's day — and steps inside a track never overlap, so anything happening *while* something else happens has to live in a different track (here the four rowers' erg work and the coach's own clock run side by side as separate tracks). Turn 4 of 4 — relationships, then the program.

Take the step list from turn 3 exactly as it stands.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else. Write your improved question out, answer it, and revise the triggers accordingly. A step the improved question reveals is added here, marked `"inferred": true`.

**Then emit the complete program JSON** in a single ```json fenced block: `schemaVersion`, `programId`, `name`, `environmentType`, `actors`, `tracks`, and a `resourceConstraints` entry for every `task` any step uses. Carry turn 3's provenance onto each step as `"metadata": {"sourceSpan": ..., "inferred": ...}`.

Then finish the job with the tools:
1. If the public catalog already covers this (search_public_recipes or start_workout), load that instead and stop — its result already has the live URL.
2. Otherwise keep the program you just built; `rhylthyme://guide/authoring` is the cheat-sheet and `rhylthyme://examples/*` are complete programs to pattern-match.
3. Express the limits as constraints, not as copied JSON: the `resourceConstraints`, `replicates`, `instances` and `maxInFlight` you confirmed in turn 2.
4. Run validate_program and fix every error it reports.
5. Run analyze_schedule to check the makespan, critical path and resource conflicts; adjust offsets so tracks finish together. Its `bindingConstraints` say which limit is actually gating the makespan.
6. Call visualize_schedule and give the user the live URL plus the Gantt/itinerary from the result. Do not describe the schedule in prose.
